title: Disable Telnet and use SSH version 2 only
description: Telnet transmits all data including credentials in cleartext. It must be disabled in favor of SSH version 2 for all remote management access to network switches.
rationale: Telnet is susceptible to eavesdropping and credential interception. SSHv2 provides encrypted communications and is required to protect management plane integrity.
check_content:
Cisco IOS: show line vty 0 15 | include Transport
Expected: Transport Input SSH (not telnet)
Verify SSHv2: show ip ssh | include version
Expected: SSH Enabled - version 2.0
fix_text:
Cisco IOS:
ip ssh version 2
line vty 0 15
 transport input ssh
 no transport input telnet
!
Aruba/HP:
ssh version 2
no telnet-server

title: Disable unused management services (HTTP, SNMP v1/v2c)
description: HTTP/HTTPS management interface should be disabled or restricted. SNMPv1 and SNMPv2c use community strings that are transmitted in cleartext and should be replaced with SNMPv3.
rationale: HTTP lacks encryption. SNMPv1/v2c community strings are easily intercepted. Leaving them enabled provides attackers with both management access and device reconnaissance capabilities.
check_content:
Cisco IOS: show running-config | include ip http|snmp-server community
HTTP/HTTPS should be absent or restricted by ACL.
SNMP community strings should not use default values (public, private).
fix_text:
Cisco IOS:
no ip http server
no ip http secure-server
no snmp-server community public
no snmp-server community private
snmp-server group <group> v3 priv
snmp-server user <user> <group> v3 auth sha <authpass> priv aes 128 <privpass>

title: Configure AAA authentication for management access
description: Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting (AAA) must be configured for all management access including console, VTY lines, and enable mode using TACACS+ or RADIUS.
rationale: Local authentication does not provide centralized audit trails. AAA with TACACS+/RADIUS enables per-command authorization and centralized logging of all management actions.
check_content:
Cisco IOS: show running-config | include aaa|tacacs|radius
Verify AAA new-model is enabled and TACACS+/RADIUS servers are configured.
Verify fallback to local is configured.
fix_text:
Cisco IOS:
aaa new-model
tacacs server <name>
 address ipv4 <tacacs-server-ip>
 key <secret>
aaa authentication login default group tacacs+ local
aaa authorization exec default group tacacs+ local
aaa accounting exec default start-stop group tacacs+

title: Set login security banner
description: A legal warning banner must be displayed before authentication on all management access methods (console, SSH, HTTPS) stating that unauthorized access is prohibited.
rationale: Login banners establish legal notice of unauthorized access prohibition, which may be required for legal action against intruders and satisfies regulatory compliance requirements.
check_content:
Cisco IOS: show running-config | include banner
Verify banner login, banner motd, or banner exec are configured with appropriate warning text.
fix_text:
Cisco IOS:
banner login ^
WARNING: Unauthorized access to this device is prohibited.
All access is monitored and logged. Disconnect immediately if not authorized.
^
banner exec ^
Authorized access only. All activity is subject to monitoring and recording.
^

title: Enable port security on access ports
description: Port security restricts the number of valid MAC addresses on a port, preventing unauthorized devices from connecting to the network through switch access ports.
rationale: Without port security, an attacker can connect an unauthorized device or hub to an access port and gain network access. MAC flooding attacks can overflow CAM tables.
check_content:
Cisco IOS: show port-security | include Enabled
For each access port: show port-security interface <interface>
Verify Maximum MAC addresses is 1 and violation mode is shutdown.
fix_text:
Cisco IOS (per access port):
interface <interface>
 switchport mode access
 switchport port-security
 switchport port-security maximum 1
 switchport port-security violation shutdown
 switchport port-security aging time 2
 switchport port-security aging type inactivity

title: Disable unused switch ports and place in unused VLAN
description: All unused switch ports must be administratively shut down and moved to a dedicated unused/quarantine VLAN that is not routed.
rationale: Unused active ports allow unauthorized physical device connections. Placing them in an unrouted VLAN prevents access to the network even if a device is connected.
check_content:
Cisco IOS: show interfaces status | include notconnect|disabled
Verify all unused ports are in 'disabled' state and assigned to a quarantine VLAN (not VLAN 1).
show running-config interface <unused-port>
fix_text:
Cisco IOS:
interface range <unused-interfaces>
 switchport access vlan 999
 shutdown
!
vlan 999
 name QUARANTINE
!

title: Disable VLAN 1 on all trunk ports and as native VLAN
description: VLAN 1 is the default VLAN and carries management and untagged traffic by default. It should not be used as the native VLAN or propagated on trunks to prevent VLAN hopping attacks.
rationale: VLAN hopping attacks exploit the native VLAN on trunk ports. Disabling VLAN 1 on trunks and changing the native VLAN to an unused VLAN prevents double-tagging attacks.
check_content:
Cisco IOS: show interfaces trunk
Verify native VLAN is not VLAN 1.
Verify VLAN 1 is not in the VLANs allowed on trunk (or is explicitly pruned).
fix_text:
Cisco IOS (per trunk port):
interface <trunk-interface>
 switchport trunk native vlan 999
 switchport trunk allowed vlan remove 1
!
Also: no vlan dot1q tag native (to tag native VLAN on Cisco switches)

title: Enable BPDU Guard on all PortFast-enabled ports
description: BPDU Guard should be enabled on all access ports configured with PortFast to prevent unauthorized switches from being connected and manipulating the spanning tree topology.
rationale: An attacker with physical access can connect a rogue switch and advertise superior BPDUs to become the root bridge, enabling traffic interception (man-in-the-middle).
check_content:
Cisco IOS: show spanning-tree summary | include BPDU Guard
Verify 'BPDU Guard Default' is enabled.
Per-interface: show spanning-tree interface <interface> detail | include BPDU
fix_text:
Cisco IOS (global):
spanning-tree portfast bpduguard default
Per interface:
interface <interface>
 spanning-tree portfast
 spanning-tree bpduguard enable

title: Configure idle session timeout on VTY lines
description: VTY (virtual terminal) lines must have an inactivity timeout configured to automatically terminate idle management sessions and prevent unauthorized access to unattended sessions.
rationale: Without session timeouts, an authenticated but abandoned session can be hijacked by an attacker with physical access to the terminal. Timeouts reduce this window.
check_content:
Cisco IOS: show running-config | section line vty
Verify 'exec-timeout 5 0' (5 minutes) or less is configured on all VTY lines.
Verify console line also has exec-timeout configured.
fix_text:
Cisco IOS:
line vty 0 15
 exec-timeout 5 0
!
line con 0
 exec-timeout 5 0
!

title: Enable logging to remote syslog server with timestamps
description: All switch events must be sent to a centralized syslog server. Log messages must include timestamps for forensic analysis and compliance reporting.
rationale: Local logs on switches may be overwritten or lost during failures. Centralized logging ensures event correlation, audit trail integrity, and timely incident detection.
check_content:
Cisco IOS: show running-config | include logging
Verify a logging host is configured, logging timestamps are enabled (service timestamps log datetime msec), and minimum severity is informational.
fix_text:
Cisco IOS:
service timestamps log datetime msec
logging <syslog-server-ip>
logging trap informational
logging source-interface <management-interface>
logging on
